title: Measure the codex workspace-write sandbox
lead: S01 never exercised codex's write block (the old #54 context says so). Before ork trusts -s workspace-write, measure it with a small spike: are writes outside the worktree and into the main checkout blocked, is .git writable, does resume keep workspace-write (the resume help lists no -s flag), and can sockets bind (known: no). This is a paid call: ask the owner for the call budget before running.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - spike scripts under spike/, fixtures under testdata/vendors/codex/, docs/design.md capability table.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Redacted fixtures record each probe and its result.
- The capability table marks the sandbox cells verified or not.
- Any gap is filed as a slice or an adj question.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
0. Stop before any call. The owner approves the call budget first. spike/common.zsh:3-4 says about six calls per vendor, and spike/codex.sh already spent four (docs/design.md:461). Three new probes take codex to seven.
1. Make the probe repo and the raw output under /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork/.scratch/s48/ (a throwaway main checkout with a linked worktree). Not the harness scratchpad.
2. Append probes 05 to 07 to spike/codex.sh after probe 04, with the probe helper from spike/common.zsh.
3. Probe 05, one call: `codex exec --json -m gpt-6-luna -s workspace-write -C WORKTREE`. Ask for three files: one in WORKTREE (positive control), one in the main checkout, one under the main checkout's .git/slicer (ledger path; ../slicer/CHANGELOG.md:134, ai.py:396-398).
4. Probe 06: `codex exec resume SID -m gpt-6-luna -s workspace-write --json`. resume-help.txt lists no -s, so record the exact error if it refuses.
5. Probe 07: ask codex to bind a Unix socket in the worktree and report the error. "Sockets cannot bind (known: no)" has no source in the ork repo; treat it as a claim to test.
6. A probe counts only if its JSONL has a command event. The fixtures show only agent_message (testdata/vendors/codex), and the command item type is unverified. Check the events before you record a result.
7. Record each probe with the same helper, so an existing .exit skips it. Save repo status for both trees with repo_status (common.zsh).
8. Run S01_DRY_RUN=1 first to write the .cmd files with no call.
9. Update docs/design.md:388-389 (resume and allowlist or sandbox cells) with what was verified. Keep vendor.codex-allowlist as decided.
10. File any gap with `adj check KEY`, then `adj ask` if open is not found. Never run adj decide.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- zsh -n spike/codex.sh spike/common.zsh (syntax).
- S01_DRY_RUN=1 zsh spike/codex.sh PROBE_REPO RAW_DIR FIX_DIR: only .cmd files change, with no vendor call.
- rg -n 'REDACTED|sk-|Bearer|/Users/jon|/private/tmp' testdata/vendors/codex: placeholders only, no secrets or paths.
- For probes 05 to 07: rg -n 'command' on the stdout fixture; each probe must show a command event.
- Read testdata/vendors/codex/05-*.repo-status: the worktree gets its file, the main checkout and .git/slicer do not, or the fixture says otherwise.
- Read the 06 and 07 exit and stderr fixtures for the resume and socket results.
- slicer check and adj lint (docs/design.md changed).
- No Go file is expected to change; if one does, run go test -race -count=1 ./..., go vet ./... and gofmt -l .
